title: Finger Zones: Index Fingers
summary: See why your index fingers cover two columns each, and which keys belong to them.

explain.goal: Learn which keys belong to your index fingers, and why they cover more than the others.
why: Each hand has five columns of keys to cover but only four typing fingers. One finger has to take two columns.
The index finger gets that job because it is the strongest, quickest, and most agile finger you have.
The keys are staggered, so each finger's column runs on a slight diagonal. The index finger covers the two columns closest to the middle of the keyboard.
After every reach, your index finger returns to its home key, F or J. Home stays your reference point.
how: Left index finger: R, T, F, G, V, B and the number keys 4 and 5.
Right index finger: Y, U, H, J, N, M and the number keys 6 and 7.
The tinted keys on the keyboard show each finger's zone. The brighter keys are F and J, the home keys.
Reach with the finger, then come straight back to F or J.

mistakes.mistake: Handing the second column to a different finger
mistakes.reason: If a middle finger reaches for G or H, it leaves its own keys, and nothing stays consistent.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the index finger away from home after a reach
mistakes.reason: Home is how you find every other key. Return to it each time.

explain.recap: Your index fingers each cover two columns because they are the strongest and most agile. Each returns to F or J after a reach.

title: Finger Zones: The Other Fingers
summary: Learn the middle, ring, and pinky zones, and why the weaker fingers need slow, accurate practice.

explain.goal: Learn the zones of your middle fingers, ring fingers, and pinkies.
why: The rest of the keyboard is split among your other six fingers, one column each. A key's column tells you its finger, so you never have to guess.
Your ring fingers and pinkies are less independent, so they feel clumsy at first. That is how hands work, and it is not a sign you are doing it wrong.
Practice them slowly and accurately instead of rushing. Speed comes after the movements are reliable.
how: Left middle: 3, E, D, C. Right middle: 8, I, K and the comma.
Left ring: 2, W, S, X. Right ring: 9, O, L and the period.
Left pinky: 1, Q, A, Z. Right pinky: 0, P, the semicolon and the slash. Your pinkies also cover the keys at the outer edges, such as the hyphen, brackets, and apostrophe.
Find each zone on the keyboard: the tinted keys are the ones a finger owns, and the bright keys are the home keys.

mistakes.mistake: Using a stronger finger to reach a key that is not its own
mistakes.reason: It feels quicker at first, but your hands never build one dependable map of the keyboard.

mistakes.mistake: Getting frustrated when the ring finger is slow
mistakes.reason: It is normal. Slow, accurate repetition is what makes it independent.

explain.recap: Every key has one finger, decided by its column. Weak fingers get better with slow, accurate practice.
